title: Charges of the basic particles
body: The elementary charge e is the magnitude of the charge of a single electron or proton and is the smallest indivisible amount of charge.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.1.iii: "The charge of an electron is −e, the charge of a proton is +e, and a neutron has no electric charge."

title: Electric field definition
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.2: "the ratio of the electric force exerted on a test charge at that point to the charge of the test charge"

title: Charged conductors in electrostatic equilibrium
body: In electrostatic equilibrium, a solid conductor's excess charge sits on its surface and the electric field inside it is zero.

items.label: Excess charge
items.meaning: distributed on the surface of the conductor

items.label: Field outside an isolated sphere with spherically symmetric charge
items.meaning: same as the field of a point charge with the sphere's net charge located at its center

ced_evidence: 10.3.B.1: "the excess charge of a solid conductor is distributed on the surface of the conductor, and the electric field within the conductor is zero"; 10.3.B.1.i; 10.3.B.1.ii

title: Equipotential (isoline) map
body: Isolines of electric potential and electric field vector maps are complementary representations, and either can be constructed from the other.

items.label: Isolines
items.meaning: lines of equal electric potential in space

items.label: Isolines vs. field vectors
items.meaning: isolines are perpendicular to electric field vectors

items.label: Field direction
items.meaning: field vectors point in the direction of decreasing potential

items.label: Field along an isoline
items.meaning: there is no component of the electric field along an isoline

ced_evidence: 10.5.B.2.i–iv: "Isolines are perpendicular to electric field vectors"; "points in the direction of decreasing potential"

title: Energy stored in a capacitor
ced_evidence: 10.6.A.5: "The electric potential energy stored in a capacitor is described by the equation"; 10.6.A.4

title: Uniform field and motion between plates
body: Between oppositely charged parallel plates the field is constant in magnitude and direction (except near the edges), so a charged particle there has constant acceleration, like projectile motion in Earth's gravitational field.
ced_evidence: 10.6.A.3 and 10.6.A.3.ii: "undergoes constant acceleration and therefore its motion shares characteristics with the projectile motion"

title: Field between charged parallel plates
caution: Valid only when the plate separation is much smaller than the plate dimensions; edge effects are ignored.
ced_evidence: 10.6.A.3.i: "where the plate separation is much smaller than the dimensions of the plates"

title: Energy conservation for a charge moving through a potential difference
caution: Applies when the electric force is the only force doing work on the charge. State that the kinetic energy change is consistent with conservation of energy.
ced_evidence: 10.7.A.2: "results in a change in kinetic energy of the object consistent with the conservation of energy"

title: Change in electric potential energy of a charge
ced_evidence: 10.7.A.1: "the resulting change in the electric potential energy of the object-field system"
